482	But this actually recalls the experience we're describing now,
483	as you stand in the Beit HaMikdash.
484	Everyone has stepped aside right now. No offerings now, no
485	incense, no other business. There's no one else
486	who is also in a hurry, who is now reading
487	the Bikurim text just to fulfill his duty and go
488	home. There's no such thing. Everyone is listening right now
489	to what you are saying.
490	And that includes all the kohanim, all the people, and even
491	the Kohen Gadol.
492	What, the Kohen Gadol? What, Rabbi? He too stands
493	and listens to a Jew who is now reciting the Bikurim text.
494	And of course, first of all, who is listening to you? The Holy
495	One, blessed be He. After all, you are in the Beit HaMikdash, in the House of HaShem.
496	The Holy One, blessed be He, also steps away from everything
497	else and listens to a Jew reciting the
498	Bikurim text.
499	And so, truly, this experience that the mitzvah of Bikurim
500	gives to a Jew
501	is an experience that, as we said before, is a
502	peak moment.
503	It's impossible to describe such a peak moment of holiness.
504	After all, we know that when we speak of the whole of Israel,
505	what is the peak moment of holiness? That the Kohen
506	Gadol, on behalf of all Israel, on the holiest day, enters the
507	Holy of Holies
508	and there atones for the whole people of Israel. But that is the Kohen
509	Gadol in the Holy of Holies.
510	But when does every Jew experience such an experience, in the connection
511	where he comes to HaShem, blessed be He, and says "You shall speak up and say"
512	before HaShem your Elokim? The Rebbe links the two things,
513	saying: on Yom Kippur it says "before HaShem you shall be purified,"
514	and in the mitzvah of Bikurim it says "before HaShem your Elokim,"
515	"you shall place the Bikurim before HaShem your Elokim."
516	So how do we understand this simply, that you are purified when you
517	come to HaShem, "before HaShem"?
518	When you bring the Bikurim, you place them
519	before HaShem. But the Alter Rebbe explains in Likutei
520	Torah that "before HaShem you shall be purified" means also, and mainly,
521	the main meaning is
522	"before," that is, above the Name Havayah Elokecha.
523	Havayah Elokecha are holy names of the Holy One,
524	blessed be He. The holiest name is the Name Havayah, but it is
525	still a name of the Holy One, blessed be He.
526	Where is a Jew able to reach? Before the Name Havayah,
527	that is, to the very essence of HaShem, blessed be He, since a Jew
528	is truly a part of Elokut from above. So when he reaches
529	the essence of the Holy One, blessed be He, he is purified, cleansed
530	of all sins, because sins do not touch and do not harm
531	the bond of a Jew with the Holy One, blessed be He.
532	In the same way, when a Jew brings the Bikurim,
533	the same words are said: "before HaShem your Elokim." That is,
534	a Jew reaches such an inner and deep experience
535	that he is now arriving like the Kohen Gadol on Yom
536	Kippur, in the Holy of Holies,
537	"before HaShem your Elokim."
538	And so we understand that the mitzvah of Bikurim is
539	truly an amazing, special, exceptional mitzvah, but
540	let's note how many conditions this mitzvah has.
541	That is why we don't, as we said, not only did we not
542	merit to fulfill it ourselves, there are not even pictures.
543	And why? Because this mitzvah can be fulfilled only
544	while the Beit HaMikdash stands.
545	And even when the Beit HaMikdash stands, it can be fulfilled only
546	between Pesach and Shavuot. Only then can a Jew bring
547	and recite the Bikurim text.
548	And even then, who can fulfill it? Only a Jew who has
549	a portion in the Land of Israel. One who lives abroad cannot
550	fulfill this mitzvah, even if amazing fruits grow for him
551	there.
552	Besides the fact that the finest fruits grow precisely
553	in the Land, but that doesn't matter: only from the Land of Israel,
554	and only if fine fruits grew for him, because one must bring from the first of the fruit of the ground.
555	>> He is obligated.
556	>> And only from the seven species. If you have what is called an orchard
557	of mango or apples or peaches, very nice,
558	but from that you cannot bring Bikurim.
559	>> People who now have... >> People who don't have the Bikurim in theirs, or
560	on their journey... >> They can't bring from someone else?
561	>> No, no, Bikurim is not a basket that you can
562	buy in a store.
563	>> A friend nearby, yes, go around...
564	>> Even if he has only some of the seven species... >> Ah.
565	>> Even only some of the seven species.
566	>> Even if he has only some of the seven species, he can bring.
567	Yes, yes, definitely, but it must be in your own portion.
568	If it's not yours, it has no meaning.
569	>> Everyone should have a portion.
570	>> Nice, of course, but what does this show us? It shows us
571	that this mitzvah has so many conditions
572	and limitations,
573	that at first glance it is a very, very particular mitzvah,
574	very unique, but very unique, meaning
575	that it is not so common and does not belong to everyone at every
576	moment and every time and every situation.
577	So this brings us back to the question:
578	why, then, does the mitzvah of Bikurim become the
579	opening
580	of the Parashah that deals with the covenant, which includes all
581	our commitment and bond with the Holy One, blessed be He,
582	through the entirety of the Torah and mitzvot, all the statutes and laws?
583	So the Rebbe explains this matter in a most
584	wonderful way, there are truly depths upon depths in it,
585	but let's try to taste something, after we drink a little.
